requirements.title: FINAL specifies a nonempty list with an optional double colon
requirements.source: 7.5.6.1, R753, R753.final-keyword, R753.optional-double-colon, R753.nonempty-name-list; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102.
requirements.definition: A final-procedure-stmt contains FINAL, an optional double colon and a nonempty final-subroutine-name-list. It occurs in the derived-type binding part under its canonical enclosing grammar. Its names designate final subroutines, not ordinary named bindings callable merely because FINAL names them.

requirements.oracle: Compile admissions distinguish the two FINAL separator spellings and a comma-separated scalar/rank-one family. Two missing-name forms are repaired by inserting finish, and a missing comma is inserted between otherwise legal distinct finals. Every target has a complete conforming module definition. Declaration acceptance is not callback execution.

requirements.title: A final subroutine has one constrained dummy of the defining type
requirements.source: 7.5.6.1, C791, C791.module-procedure, C791.exactly-one-dummy, C791.nonoptional-dummy, C791.noncoarray-dummy, C791.nonpointer-dummy, C791.nonallocatable-dummy, C791.nonpolymorphic-variable, C791.type-being-defined, C791.all-lengths-assumed, C791.no-intent-out, C791.no-value; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102.
requirements.definition: A named final subroutine must be a module procedure with exactly one dummy argument. That dummy is a nonoptional, noncoarray, nonpointer, nonallocatable, nonpolymorphic variable of the type being defined, with every length parameter assumed and neither INTENT(OUT) nor VALUE. KIND parameters and rank retain their separate selection/uniqueness rules.

pending.dummy-kind-and-interface-use-graph: Pending canonical dummy-data-object versus dummy-procedure, abstract-type, shape, import, purity and passed-interface relationships; do not claim one scalar declaration covers all such contexts.

requirements.oracle: Five compile admissions exercise scalar, assumed-shape, separate module, assumed-rank and IMPURE ELEMENTAL finals. Thirteen source-minimal pairs isolate external-versus-module selection, dummy count, each prohibited attribute/category and each of two nonassumed LEN values. The external pair changes only its FINAL name, retains explicit interface/IMPORT and complete same-type definitions, and does not rely on a prior missing module. The zero-dummy repair adds signature and declaration together; the removed second dummy remains a legal plain INTEGER local. Coarray syntax is explicit with no dummy SAVE; VALUE uses INTENT(IN). No finalizer body executes.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A name labelled final-subroutine-name does not make a function legal. Preserve the exact module-procedure and dummy-variable roles; overlapping defects must remain explicit rather than being advertised as isolated. Every prospective negative needs a complete otherwise conforming source and a source-minimal repair, with a primary diagnostic identifying the actual final procedure, dummy or signature condition. Required reporting need not be fatal. Wrong-subject recovery, missing facilities, crashes and resource errors are not that cause. No message, compiler result or approval is claimed.

requirements.title: A type cannot specify the same final subroutine again
requirements.source: 7.5.6.1, C792, C792.same-type-scope, C792.not-previously-specified; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102.
requirements.definition: A final-subroutine-name must not denote a final subroutine already specified for that type. This is repetition within one defining type, not a ban on final subroutines of other types or a substitute for signature uniqueness.

requirements.oracle: One compile admission and three duplicate-name pairs use the same actual module final identity, including case-equivalent spelling. List repairs remove one occurrence. The repeated-statement repair removes the whole redundant FINAL statement rather than leaving a bare FINAL. Distinct source scopes are not merged by textual basename.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not infer duplicate procedure identity solely from a matching textual basename across scopes. Every prospective negative needs a complete otherwise conforming source and a source-minimal repair, with a primary diagnostic identifying the actual final procedure, dummy or signature condition. Required reporting need not be fatal. Wrong-subject recovery, missing facilities, crashes and resource errors are not that cause. No message, compiler result or approval is claimed.

requirements.title: Final subroutine signatures are unique by KIND tuple and rank
requirements.source: 7.5.6.1, C793, C793.another-final-of-same-type, C793.equal-kind-parameters, C793.equal-rank; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102.
requirements.definition: Two final subroutines of the same type must not have dummies with both equal kind type parameter values and equal rank. A different name or different implementation body does not distinguish that signature. LEN values are not a discriminator and are already required to be assumed by C791.

requirements.oracle: Compile-only rank and abstract-KIND families are independently legal. Equal scalar signatures are repaired by changing only the second rank. The two-KIND tuple case has independent one-coordinate repairs, with LEN remaining assumed and no intrinsic representation selector. The ordinary/IMPURE ELEMENTAL scalar conflict is repaired by making only the ordinary dummy an array. No payload, dispatch or callback count is observed.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A TYPE/CLASS difference, fixed LEN change or invalid elemental array dummy is not a legal repair for the same-signature condition. requirements.title: An assumed-rank final excludes every other same-KIND final
requirements.source: 7.5.6.1, C794, C794.assumed-rank-condition, C794.no-same-kind-other-final; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102.
requirements.definition: When a final subroutine has an assumed-rank dummy, the type must have no other final subroutine with the same kind type parameter values. A different fixed rank alone does not satisfy this condition.

requirements.oracle: A sole assumed-rank final and a different-KIND assumed-rank/fixed-rank family have compile admissions. Three same-KIND conflicts pair assumed rank with scalar, vector or legal IMPURE ELEMENTAL scalar finals. Each repair removes the whole competing FINAL statement while preserving both valid procedure bodies. Rank distinction is not used to evade same-KIND exclusivity; no runtime precedence or assumed-rank payload query is inferred.

requirements.title: Finalizability is a recursive type and nonpointer-entity classification
requirements.source: 7.5.6.1, p2, p2.type-has-final-subroutine, p2.plain-finalizable-component, p2.nonpointer-data-entity, p2.entity-type-condition, p2.all-other-entities-excluded; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102.
requirements.definition: A derived type is finalizable exactly when it has a final subroutine or a nonpointer nonallocatable component of finalizable type. A nonpointer data entity is finalizable exactly when its type is finalizable; no other entity is finalizable. A pointer entity and its target are different, and allocated allocatable subobjects can be finalized by their own deallocation events without making the containing type finalizable through this recursion.

requirements.oracle: Classification requires reviewed source/use relations, not a fabricated runtime inquiry or a no-op parser success. Concrete users have separately declared events and independently initialized observable state.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No mandatory callback follows merely from a finalizable type: selection and event conditions remain separate. Allocatable-component cleanup and unreachable pointer-target choices are not collapsed into the recursive classification.
